mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where UNRATE remains below 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of episodes where INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over a two-month window indicates a successful disinflationary tightening, which supports equity valuations by reducing inflation risk premia and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND RSAFS > 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of episodes where both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month MA for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for four consecutive months signals a significant loosening of the labor market, which reduces wage growth and input costs, ultimately supporting corporate margins and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of episodes where UNRATE exceeds 6% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which drags on construction-related and material sector earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of episodes where HOUST is below its 12-month MA for eight months.
